question: Without expanding, show that $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&3\\2&3&4\\3&4&5\end{vmatrix}=0$. State the relation among its rows that justifies the result.
explanation:
Relation among the rows
Let the rows of the determinant be denoted by $R_1$, $R_2$ and $R_3$. Their elements show that $$R_1+R_3=\begin{bmatrix}4&6&8\end{bmatrix}=2R_2$$
Linear dependence of rows
Thus, $$R_1-2R_2+R_3=0$$ Therefore, the three rows are linearly dependent.
Zero-determinant property
If the rows of a determinant are linearly dependent, its value is zero. Equivalently, applying $R_3\to R_3-2R_2+R_1$ produces a complete row of zeros.
Conclusion
Hence, without direct expansion, $$\begin{vmatrix}1&2&3\\2&3&4\\3&4&5\end{vmatrix}=0$$
